output.hypothesis: Freelancers invoicing international clients will open a Wise account when shown specific currency coverage (22 currencies with local account details), concrete speed metrics (96% under 24 hours), and peer adoption evidence from similar freelancers on LinkedIn and Medium.

calls.reason: Find past campaign evidence about freelancer-specific messaging, currency coverage claims, and speed metrics that drove account openings
Understand previous campaign goals, editorial scores, and fact/claim patterns for Wise freelancer campaigns
Measure which content types and platforms (LinkedIn, Medium) historically drove account openings for Wise
Check if past claims about currency coverage, payment speed, and freelancer benefits were verified or flagged
Identify specific claims about Wise freelancer features that failed verification to avoid repeating them
Identify what freelancer audiences actually engage with on platforms regarding international payments and Wise

decisions.statement: Do not use time-bound claims about payment speed or fee structures without current verification; 8 time-bound claims remain unverified and 9 framing claims need editorial review.
decisions.rationale: claim_risk#2 shows 8 time-bound claims in time-sensitive status unrepaired; claim_risk#1 shows 9 framing claims in editorial status.

decisions.statement: Capability claims about Wise Business features are supported and safe to use; 4 capability claims verified.
decisions.rationale: claim_risk#3 shows 4 capability claims with supported status and 0 repaired.

decisions.statement: Build content around the verified 22-currency account details and specific currency list (AUD, CAD, EUR, GBP, HUF, NZD, PHP, SGD, USD) for receiving payments like a local.
decisions.rationale: fact:fact-2 confirms 22 currencies with global account details; fact:fact-5 lists 9 specific currencies available for local receiving.

decisions.statement: Use the 96% under-24-hours payment speed metric as a core proof point for freelancers invoicing international clients.
decisions.rationale: fact:fact-8 states 96% of payments to international partners take less than 24 hours.

decisions.statement: Target freelancers who need to receive payments in multiple currencies and value payment admin simplicity; avoid US-based freelancers needing business cards due to deactivation signals.
decisions.rationale: fact:fact-17 and fact:fact-15 position Wise Business for international payment admin; audience_signals#3 shows US Business card deactivation with 56 points/48 comments.

decisions.statement: Do not mention Wise Business cards for US audiences or imply card availability in the US; the deactivation notice is a live community concern.
decisions.rationale: audience_signals#3 documents Wise deactivating Business cards in the US on Oct 31st with significant community discussion (56 points, 48 comments).

decisions.statement: Lead with 'payment admin painless' messaging: combine 22-currency local account details, 96% sub-24-hour speed, and free same-currency receipt to show total workflow relief.
decisions.rationale: fact:fact-17 quotes 'making payment admin painless'; fact:fact-2 and fact:fact-8 provide the concrete metrics; fact:fact-24 confirms free receipt.

decisions.statement: Prioritize LinkedIn for professional freelancer audiences; Medium performance data unavailable so treat as secondary until measured.
decisions.rationale: Platforms specified are LinkedIn and Medium; performance tool returned no rows for either platform, so no evidence to prioritize Medium.
